history.summary: Added deterministic dual API-key/session authentication with explicit-credential conflict rejection, shared credential-aware CSRF selection, unchanged RBAC and JSON API behavior, and session-only first-party HTTP transport. Removed the API key from common browser state while retaining its dedicated settings and API management exposure, regenerated reproducible assets, and added exhaustive middleware, controller, browser, Docker, documentation, and regression evidence. Full verification, race, browser, production-container, dependency, and security scanner gates completed with no new finding.

All 26 acceptance criteria verified satisfied. Shared extractor used by both API auth and CSRF. Explicit credential mechanism selected before validation with no fallback. Session auth succeeds when no explicit credential present. Invalid/empty/ambiguous explicit credentials always fail (401), never inherit session authority. RBAC and error parity preserved through unchanged middleware chain. Frontend transport decoupled from API keys (same-origin cookies, no Authorization header, no global exposure). CSRF protection properly aware of credential type: session requests protected, explicit API keys remain exempt. Comprehensive test coverage across middleware, controller, browser, and real Docker container. All quality gates passed. No credential leaks in errors or logs. Plaintext storage and settings exception documented honestly.
Session API access bypasses forced password change, and campaign completion mutates through GET without session CSRF or view-only enforcement.

Blocked forced-password-change sessions from API access with JSON errors before handlers or RBAC while preserving explicit API-key compatibility. Moved session campaign completion to POST so existing CSRF and view-only enforcement apply, rejected session GET without mutation, retained explicit API-key GET compatibility, audited other GET handlers, and added focused, browser, Docker, documentation, and regression coverage. Full verification, race, reproducibility, container, dependency, and security scanner gates completed with no new finding.

Both security review findings independently verified fixed. Password-change requirement now blocks session API access with 403 JSON before handler/RBAC while API-key path unaffected. Campaign completion moved to POST with same-origin/CSRF/view-only enforcement; session GET rejected deterministically via non-forgeable auth-mechanism marker while explicit-key GET retained. All other API GET endpoints audited—campaign completion only mutating GET. Auth-mechanism marker correctly set only post-auth, cannot be forged. Full quality gates passed. Iteration 1 criteria preserved. No new issues.
Final specialist re-review found no remaining high-confidence authentication, CSRF, authorization, or exposure issue.
Final complete-diff review and focused auth/session/frontend/Docker tests found no significant issue.
